EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours have seen a significant escalation in the Iran war, characterized by intense US-Israeli airstrikes deep within Iran targeting critical infrastructure and military leadership, alongside retaliatory ballistic missile attacks on Israel from Iran, Yemen, and Lebanon. The destruction of Iran's strategic B1 bridge near Karaj and the shutdown of its largest steel producer mark a severe blow to Iranian capabilities, while high-level US military dismissals hint at internal strategic divergences.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran have intensified. The IDF reported completing approximately 20 airstrikes in central and western Iran within the past day, dropping over 140 bombs on more than 50 ballistic missile targets, including launchers, using F-35i fighter jets. Targets included a base of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Ground Forces in Tehran, mobile command centers where commanders operated, and a ballistic missile storage site in Tabriz. The US military is reported to have attacked the strategic B1 bridge connecting Tehran and Karaj, which it claims was a supply route for Iran's missile and drone industries. Iranian sources confirm the destruction of the B1 bridge, reporting 8 civilian deaths and 95 injuries, and subsequent power outages in the Alborz province, including on the Chalous road. Other reported targets in Iran include Mashhad airport's fuel depot, Kashan airport, Qom's police headquarters and Khaybar base, Shiraz's electronics industries and Sarallah base, Borazjan's missile site, and the Bakardian base in Behbahan.

Iranian military leadership has sustained casualties, with the IDF confirming the elimination of Mukram Azimi, commander of the ballistic missile unit in Kermanshah responsible for numerous launches towards Israel, and Jamshid Eshaghi, chief of Iran's "oil headquarters" overseeing funding for military buildup and proxies. Mohammad Ali Fathali-Zadeh, commander of the Fatehin unit of the IRGC ground forces, was also reported killed.
In retaliation, Iran launched approximately 20 ballistic missiles at Israel in the past day, with some carrying cluster bomb warheads. The IRGC also claimed to have struck the USS Abraham Lincoln with four Ghadr missiles and targeted an Oracle data center in the UAE and an Amazon cloud computing center in Bahrain, warning of further action against tech companies involved in "terror operations." Iranian air defenses claimed to have shot down an advanced US F-35 over central Iran and another "enemy" fighter jet near Qeshm Island, though CENTCOM denied these claims, stating all US aircraft were accounted for.

Economically, the Mobarakeh Steel Company, Iran's largest steel producer, has completely shut down, halting all production lines due to attacks. Global oil prices surged above $140/barrel, the highest since 2008, with warnings they could reach $200. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi indicated plans to determine transit fees for ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has declared closed for US and Israeli vessels. Internally, protestor Amir Hossein Hatami, 18, was executed, and there are reports of Basij forces hiding motorcycles in children's playgrounds, allegedly to claim civilian targeting if attacked. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian engaged in diplomatic calls, reiterating Iran's right to self-defense and criticizing the EU's response to the conflict.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included extensive airstrikes against Iranian ballistic missile infrastructure, with the IDF confirming 20 strike missions hitting over 50 targets with 140 bombs. Significant targets eliminated include Mukram Azimi, commander of Iran's ballistic missile unit in Kermanshah, and Jamshid Eshaghi, head of Iran's "oil headquarters" responsible for financing military and proxy groups. In Gaza, the IDF conducted drone strikes in the Mawasi area, killing four Hamas operatives, and further strikes in Jabalia and Khan Younis killed three and two low-ranking Hamas operatives respectively. On the northern border, two Nahal Brigade soldiers were lightly injured in a close-range clash with a Hezbollah operative in southern Lebanon, who was subsequently killed.

The Israeli home front experienced sustained missile attacks. Iran launched approximately 20 ballistic missiles, some with cluster bomb warheads, causing minor injuries to several people and property damage in central Israel, including Petah Tikva and Ramat Gan. One person was also lightly injured in Mazkeret Batya. The Iran-backed Houthis claimed responsibility for ballistic missile attacks targeting the Tel Aviv area, with one missile intercepted after triggering sirens in Jerusalem and near the Dead Sea. Hezbollah launched over 130 rockets from Lebanon, with more than 50 rockets fired this morning alone, resulting in two people lightly injured in Kiryat Shmona and two in Bi'ina, and damage to a daycare in Nahariya. Air defense systems intercepted some missiles and rockets, while others hit open areas. Sirens were activated across numerous areas, including Kiryat Shmona, Metulla, Tel-Hai, Malkia, Kfar Yuval, Dishon, Gush Dan, Sharon, Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and the Dead Sea. Home Front Command issued instructions for residents to leave protected areas after incidents concluded.

Politically, Defense Minister Israel Katz issued a strong threat to Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem, stating he would "pay a very heavy price." Education Minister Yoav Kisch reported an attempted break-in at his home during a siren, attributing it to "anarchists" and criticizing the prosecution. Reports indicate Prime Minister Netanyahu's continued reliance on Aryeh Deri for coalition stability.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Ground operations in Gaza included an IDF drone strike in the Mawasi area, killing four Hamas operatives. Additional strikes in Jabalia (northern Gaza) and Khan Younis resulted in the deaths of three and two Hamas operatives, respectively. Palestinian media reported artillery fire east of Khan Younis. A militant successfully infiltrated an IDF outpost in Gaza but was subsequently eliminated. No specific information regarding the humanitarian situation, ceasefire negotiations, or settler activity was available in the provided messages.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations have been extensive, with the group firing over 130 rockets into Israel in the past day. More than 50 rockets were launched this morning, impacting areas such as the Krayot suburbs of Haifa, Bi'ina, Nahariya, Kiryat Shmona, Malkia, Yir'on, and Misgav Am. Two men were lightly injured in Bi'ina by a Hezbollah rocket, and two people were lightly injured in Kiryat Shmona. Drones were also reported to have attacked northern settlements in Israel.

Israeli strikes targeted Hezbollah forces and infrastructure. The IDF announced the killing of over 40 Hezbollah operatives in the past day and more than 1,000 since hostilities escalated, including hundreds from the elite Radwan Force. Dozens of Hezbollah command centers, weapon depots, rocket launchers, and anti-tank missile launch posts were bombed by the Israeli Air Force. The Israeli Navy also struck a Hezbollah weapons depot. An face-to-face engagement in southern Lebanon resulted in Nahal Brigade soldiers killing a Hezbollah operative, with two Israeli soldiers lightly injured. Hostile aircraft intrusion alerts and frequent rocket sirens were reported along the northern Israeli border.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Militia activity in Iraq remains high. The Islamic Resistance of Iraq claimed to have carried out 23 operations in the past 24 hours, using dozens of drones and missiles against "enemy bases" in Iraq and the broader region. Pro-Iranian militias in Iraq reported three of their members killed in an airstrike, including a senior commander named Yasin Mohammad Sadeq (Abu Taha). The US military conducted attacks against pro-Iranian militias in northern Iraq, near Mosul, reportedly injuring at least three individuals. A drone attack also targeted a US logistical center in Baghdad, causing property damage. The US Embassy in Baghdad issued a warning to American citizens to leave Iraq, citing the possibility of pro-Iranian militia attacks in the central capital within the next 24-48 hours.

In Erbil, airstrikes targeted positions of Kurdish groups PJAK and Komala. Additionally, the US Consulate in Erbil was reportedly attacked by drones. The Iraqi Ministry of Foreign Affairs reiterated Iraq's stance on maintaining distance from regional conflicts and preventing its territory from being used for hostile actions.

GULF STATES
The Gulf States continue to be impacted by and respond to the ongoing conflict. Iran's IRGC claimed strikes on a US tech giant Oracle data center in the United Arab Emirates and an Amazon cloud computing center in Bahrain, warning of further actions against companies perceived as supporting hostile operations. In Kuwait, the Mina Al-Ahmadi refinery was reportedly targeted by suicide drones, leading to multiple explosions. Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman held discussions with Russian President Putin. Press TV claimed that an Iranian missile strike destroyed a US AN/TPY-2 radar at Saudi Arabia’s Prince Sultan Air Base, resulting in one American soldier's death, though this remains unverified by other sources. A US base in Qatar was also reported to be under missile and drone attack.

Diplomatically, the UAE issued a formal statement affirming Iranian residents as an integral part of its society and committing to maintaining a safe environment. Separately, the UAE is reportedly considering supporting a US-led operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister stated that Iran is drafting a joint protocol with Oman for transit oversight in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, with its closure threatening global food and energy prices, according to the UN Secretary-General. The UN Security Council meeting scheduled to vote on a Bahrain-proposed resolution to reopen the Strait was postponed. Russia, China, and France blocked an Arab-backed initiative at the UNSC to authorize military action to reopen the strait, citing opposition to any use of force. French President Macron deemed a military operation in Hormuz "not realistic," while the EU's Foreign Minister Kaja Kallas suggested expanding the EU's naval task force for safe passage. Russia affirmed the Strait of Hormuz is open to its vessels.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Intensified US-Israeli Strikes on Iran**: Over 50 ballistic missile targets, an IRGC Ground Forces base, and mobile command centers in Iran were hit by approximately 140 bombs in the past day. The strategic B1 bridge between Tehran and Karaj was destroyed, with Iranian reports indicating 8 civilian deaths and 95 injuries.
2.  **Iranian Military Leadership Eliminated**: The IDF confirmed killing Mukram Azimi, commander of Iran's Kermanshah ballistic missile unit, and Jamshid Eshaghi, chief of Iran's "oil headquarters" responsible for funding proxies. Mohammad Ali Fathali-Zadeh, commander of the Fatehin unit, was also reported killed.
3.  **Widespread Iranian Retaliation**: Iran launched approximately 20 ballistic missiles at Israel, some carrying cluster bomb warheads causing minor injuries. The IRGC also claimed strikes on US tech/computing centers in the UAE and Bahrain.
4.  **Escalation on Northern Israeli Border**: Hezbollah fired over 130 rockets into northern Israel, injuring several, including two men in Bi'ina and two people in Kiryat Shmona, and causing damage to a daycare in Nahariya.
5.  **Critical Iranian Infrastructure Damage**: Mobarakeh Steel Company, Iran's largest steel producer, ceased all production, and Mashhad airport's fuel depot was extensively damaged.
6.  **Strait of Hormuz Stalemate**: Russia, China, and France blocked an Arab-backed UN Security Council resolution to authorize military action to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran announced plans to impose transit fees for vessels.
7.  **US Military Leadership Purge**: US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth dismissed Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George and two other senior generals (Hodne, Green Jr.), amid reports of internal disagreements regarding the Iran war strategy.
8.  **Regional Proxy Operations**: Iran-backed Houthis claimed ballistic missile attacks on the Tel Aviv area, and the Islamic Resistance of Iraq reported 23 operations against US bases in Iraq.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of escalation is critically high, driven by direct US-Israeli strikes on deep Iranian military and civilian-economic infrastructure and Iran's extensive retaliatory attacks against Israel and US assets in the Gulf. Active flashpoints include the Iranian mainland (missile sites, industrial facilities), the Israeli home front (ongoing missile threats from Iran, Yemen, and Lebanon), the Israel-Lebanon border (daily clashes, high Hezbollah activity), Iraq (militia attacks on US forces), and the Strait of Hormuz (blockade, potential for military intervention).
Military posture changes include Iran's adaptation to strikes by utilizing mobile command centers and US reports of deploying A-10 Warthogs to the Middle East. Red lines are being tested or crossed by all parties: Iran considers attacks on its civilian infrastructure and cultural sites as war crimes, while US President Trump's threats of further destruction of Iranian power plants and bridges exacerbate this perception. Iran's explicit targeting of US tech companies and military assets in the Gulf introduces new dimensions to the conflict. The high-level dismissals within the US military suggest significant internal strategic disagreements that could impact future operations.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States**: President Trump threatened further destruction in Iran, specifically targeting bridges and power plants, and suggested Iran wants a deal. He oversaw significant changes in his administration, including the dismissal of Attorney General Pam Bondi, Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George, and two other generals. He also announced a $1.5 trillion defense budget. The US Embassy in Baghdad advised American citizens to leave Iraq due to potential militia attacks.
**Gulf States**: The UAE issued a statement affirming the value of Iranian residents and is reportedly exploring support for a US-led operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke with Russian President Putin.
**European Union Members**: Russia, China, and France collectively blocked an Arab-backed UN Security Council resolution to authorize military action to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. French President Macron stated that a military operation in the Strait of Hormuz is "not realistic." Austria refused US requests for its airspace for Iran operations, citing neutrality. Finland's President urged a ceasefire and diplomatic solutions in a call with Iranian President Pezeshkian. EU Foreign Minister Kaja Kallas suggested expanding the EU naval task force to ensure safe passage in Hormuz.
**Russia**: Foreign Minister Lavrov condemned military aggression against Iran and advocated for diplomacy. Russia's nuclear agency plans to request a ceasefire to evacuate staff from the Bushehr nuclear power plant. A Putin aide confirmed the Strait of Hormuz remains open for Russian vessels. Russia is also reportedly engaged in "intelligence diplomacy" with the CIA to manage the Iran crisis.
**China**: China's Foreign Ministry attributed the closure of the Strait of Hormuz to US and Israeli strikes against Iran, justifying Iran's actions.
**Japan**: A shipment of 400 Tomahawk missiles from the US to Japan has been delayed due to the "Iran war."
**United Nations**: The UN Secretary-General expressed grave concern over the Middle East crisis entering its second month, highlighted increased human suffering, and stressed the need to respect sovereignty, protect civilians, and ensure freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. He called on the US and Israel to halt the war and Iran to cease attacks on its neighbors.
**Argentina**: Expelled Iran's charge d'affaires.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims were observed. The IRGC's claims of shooting down a US F-35 and another advanced fighter jet over Iran and near Qeshm Island were explicitly denied by CENTCOM, which stated all US aircraft were accounted for. While US military reports confirmed striking targets in Iran, the IDF explicitly denied striking the B1 bridge near Karaj, even though Trump posted video footage of its destruction and it was attributed to the US by other sources, indicating a potential distinction between US and Israeli operational claims or a lack of clarity in reporting.

Unverified claims include Press TV's report of an American soldier killed in an Iranian missile strike on a US radar base in Saudi Arabia, and IRGC claims of hitting the USS Abraham Lincoln and US tech/computing centers in the UAE and Bahrain, for which independent corroboration is lacking.

Propaganda indicators are prevalent on both sides. Iranian state media heavily emphasized civilian casualties from the B1 bridge attack and framed US/Israeli actions as war crimes, while the IRGC's exaggerated claims of shoot-downs serve to project strength. Trump's bellicose rhetoric threatening further destruction and demanding a "deal" with Iran also reflects a clear propaganda effort. The reported tactic by Basij forces of hiding motorcycles in playgrounds, if accurate, would be a clear attempt to manipulate narratives around civilian targeting.

Reporting gaps include a lack of independent verification for casualty figures in Iran and precise details on the extent and nature of damage from US/Israeli strikes. Information on the humanitarian situation in Gaza remains sparse. The long-term impacts of the Strait of Hormuz situation beyond initial oil price spikes and diplomatic maneuvering are not yet clear. There is no information from Turkey in the provided messages.
